steps.text: In a large heavy saucepan, melt butter over medium heat; add orzo and brown until golden.
Add rice, bouillon, and water; bring to a boil, cover and lower heat to medium-low.
Simmer for about 20 to 25 minutes or until all water is absorbed; serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Orzo and Rice
raw_recipe.description: An orzo rice dish. Orzo pasta, toasted golden brown in butter, is cooked in bouillon with rice to make an easy and versatile side. Garnish with herbs.
raw_recipe.name: Orzo and Rice

recipeInstructions.text: In a large heavy saucepan, melt butter over medium heat; add orzo and brown until golden.
Add rice, bouillon, and water; bring to a boil, cover and lower heat to medium-low.
Simmer for about 20 to 25 minutes or until all water is absorbed; serve.

review.reviewBody: Some reviewers have called this bland - I say it's mild, which sometimes is just what is called for to complement what it's served with. If this were a main dish I might agree it would be missing something substantial, but as a side dish it complemented, rather than competed with, the main dish. That said, I still "enhanced" it just a bit - I browned the rice along with the orzo, cooked it in chicken broth as well as the bouillon, and added another couple of tablespoons of butter and a tiny pinch of saffron. Just before serving I stirred in a little chopped fresh parsley for freshness and color. A really enjoyable side dish that's bound to make its way to my table again.

I thought this was really good, but I put a spin on it that came out really good. Heat 2-3 Tbs of oil over medium heat I added 1/2 cup finely chopped onion and 2 crushed garlic cloves and sautéed for a few minutes stirring occasionally. Then I added 1 cup of Orzo and 1 cup of white rice and stirred it all together for a few more minutes. I then mixed in 4 sprigs of chopped cilantro. I added 4 cups of boxed chicken broth, brought it to a simmer, covered it and put it over the lowest heat possible for 20 minutes.....it was delish! I served it along side of Picadillo and plantains...

Delicious. Only change I made was to use 1 tsp Knorr boullion POWDER instead of the cube, and after lightly browning the orzo I add the rice and keep stirring until the rice starts to turn opaque -- THEN add the water and the boullion.

This was very good! (went fast!) I did a HUGE variation on it because I was really going for a risotto dish, but I used this recipe as a base, and what the others suggested. I cooked some diced chicken, put it off to the side, browned onion and garlic and then the rice (3/4c each) in white wine. Poured in Chicken stock and put in my spices. Let that sit for about 30-40 min. Added fresh parmesan cheese. It got nice and thick. added the chicken and even put in some proscuitto (thinly sliced)!! Put more cheese...! It was super yummy. I'm not big on the bouillon, but it's a good recipe regardless. Everyone has their own tastes though, it's easy to put variation on it! Recommended with creativity!

Oh this was soo easy to make. It was fabulous. I had to make a massive batch for 6 growing kids and my husband. And everyone loved it. I didn't change anything when it came to the recipe or ingredients. Only the change of steps. I have a rice cooker and needed space to cook on the stove. So I did the melting of the butter and browning of the orzo in a skillet, then transferred all the ingredients to my rice cooker, stirred really well and let the rice cooker do it's job. I had no problem with it turning out. Matter of fact it stayed moist and fluffy. And the flavor was really great. I would have done chicken broth instead of bouillon but I had some better then bouillon paste, that made it just rich with flavor and it was awesome. Thanks.

I loved the change with having these two together..I did sauté some onion, garlic and shredded carrot before putting in the rice cooker
I also used vegetable broth
Could be
Vegan if u use an alternate to the butter

I found this to be an simple recipe that can easily be tailored to individual preference. Based on other reviews, I added 1 shredded carrot, 2 green onions and 1 clove of garlic, which I sautéed after the orzo was browned. I substituted water and bullion with 1 can chicken broth. I served this with ‘best green bean casserole’ (from this site) and baked chicken. It’s a keeper!
I added unsalted chicken stock with bouillon powder, parsley flakes, dill weed, onion and garlic powder and bay leaf it was very flavorful the kosher salt enhanced all flavors

Definitely agree with the 'bland' reviews, but I like Rice A Roni, and this is definitely homemade RAR. I sprinkled with salt, pepper, poultry seasoning, garlic powder, and smoked paprika, and that helped. Next time, I will use chicken broth in place of the water. Overall, a good base for a side dish that can be customized in many ways with add-ins, etc.

I give this four stars bc I did have to make a few changes. I sautéed a few onions with the orzo and used 2 cups of Swanson's chicken stock instead of the water and bullion cube. I also put a dash or two of garlic salt. It was just like rice a roni and went well with chicken. I also added some parmesean cheese to the finished product and it was yummy too. I like this recipe bc its so basic and you can pretty much just dress it up with whatever you feel like on that night.

This is a very good side dish. I'm glad I took others advice to add a little more seasoning or it would have been bland. I added garlic and onion while I was browning the orzo, and I used one can of chicken broth and 2 bouillon cubes and water to supplement the rest (I did double the recipe). It was very tasty, and even with the extra flavor added, it was a mild dish. Very good.
This went well with chicken, along with the obligatory green beans and corn. We also made a quick packet of Knorr hollandaise sauce to go with it. Just right!
I just made this today. So good. I added some ground pepper, and when done, added some minced cilantro. Even better.
I love this recipe! I have made many times and is addicting! I love it with fish, chicken, pork, you name it! Just add a herb to accent your main dish!❤😎
Tasty and easy. Kids liked it!
I always use bone broth vs bouillon. Much more flavorful and better for you. I'd recommend throwing a few extra spices to add more flavor, as well.
I added parsley. It’s definitely a good starter recipe to add things to I give it a definite thumbs up.
Added cooked ground beef and beef bouillon instead of chicken bouillon. Also hot sauce.

I made a couple changes, like I do with almost every recipe I find. I sauteed minced garlic with the orzo and rice in the butter before adding the chicken broth, which I made with extra chicken bouillon and added lots of onion powder. It tasted great and was fairly easy. Only problem was after 15 minutes it was starting to burn, granted those bits, when scrapped off, where even tastier than the rest.

Some people call it bland. Yes, as written it can be a little bland. But that is what makes it so good to go with everything and anything. Love this recipe. It’s a basic Rice a Roni and you can season it up anyway you want. Or make it as written to go with something saucy.
